 Judgment
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 16.112.2021 at about 3.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.ME4JC589JET283740 slowly and cautiously on the correct side of the road, when he reached near Hogalagere cross, on Hogalagere- Srinivasapura road, Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, one Maruthi car bearing registration No.KA-51-MF-4328 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital,
Srinivasapura wherein he took the first aid treatment, then he was shifted to Narendra Hospital,
Kolar wherein he was treated as an inpatient and had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicines,
attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 28 years, working as a mason and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and he used to spend the said amount for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-51-MF-4328.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Srinivasapura Police in Crime No.213/2021 under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After registration of the case, notices were issued to the respondents.

In response to the notices,
the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.

sentences.text: In the written statement of the respondent No.2, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But it is the strong contention of the respondent No.2 that the petitioner was riding unnumbered motor cycle without driving licence and himself fallen on the road and sustained injuries.
Hence, it is a self accident.
The car was not at all involved in the accident.
It is also the contention of the respondent that the car was used without having valid registration certificate, permit and fitness certificate.
Further contended that the respondent No.1 has not complied the mandatory provisions of under section 134(c) & Section 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident,
that was taken place on 16.121.2021 at about 3.30 p.m. near Hogalagere cross, On Hogalagere- Srinivasapura road, Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District, due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Maruthi Alto Car bearing registration No.KA-51-MF- 4328, in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3) What order or award?
9.

10.

At the same time, the respondent No.1 being owner of the offending vehicle placed exparte.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
12.

 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-51-MF- 4328, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed the involvement of the car bearing No.KA-51-MF-4328.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle placed exparte.
In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
15. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.

16. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Muniraju, the S.H.O. of Srinivasapura Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279, & 337 of I.P.C.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

17 In answer to the evidence of the petitioner the respondent company relied on the evidence of Legal Executive by name Aishwarya Rao S.M., who examined as RW1, at the time of her evidence stated that on perusal of the police documents viz., spot mahazar and IMV report discloses that there is contributory negligence of both the vehicles.
Hence, the petitoner has contributed for the cause of accident.
In support of her evidence relied on only insurance policy marked at Ex.R1 for consideation.
To prove the defense of the rash and negligenct act of the petitioner, no convincing documents placed on record for consideration.

Either to examine the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witnesses who witnessed the alleged accident to prove that there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.

18. Though the PW1 was subjected to cross- examination at length, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

From the oral evidence of the PW1 coupled with the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P6, it is clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident which is result of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-51-MF-4328.

ISSUE NO.2 :
19.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

20. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1)Sign and symptom fracture upper end of tibia comminuted and compound I 2) Fracture of both bones of right forearm 3) Complete avulsion great toe right (dip joint) great toe right with skin attachment 22.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the aforesaid injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P7.
On going through the discharge summary of Narendra Hopital, Kolar reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 16.12.2021 to 26.12.2021.
In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.S.A.Somashekar as PW2.
PW2 has placed clinical note & x-ray as per Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.

By taking Krishna N vs Srinivas N on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65379443/
5 into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.

Loss of income during treatment period:
23.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a mason and was earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not placed any iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner.
In such a situation, as per law, notional income has to be taken.
On going through the discharge summary of Narendra Hopital, Kolar reveals that, the petitioner was admitted from 16.12.2021 to 26.12.2021.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of three months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.45,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
24.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.1,65,965/- as per Ex.P9 along with prescriptions as per Ex.P10.
At the time of cross-examination except the suggestion that the medical bills are created, nothing has been placed on record to prove that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,65,965/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
25.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
26.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P5 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
To substantiate this, the petitioner had placed discharge summary for consideration.

Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr. S.A.
Somashekar examined as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones of right forearm, type I compound fracture proximal 1/3rd of right tibia (right Krishna N vs Srinivas N on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65379443/
6 leg), great toe avulsion right foot with loss of vascularity.

Petitioner undergone surgery in the form of open reduction and internal fixation with DC plating and screws for forearm on 18.12.2021, open reduction and internal fixation with locking plate and screws for right tibia on 20.12.2021 and amputation of right foot great toe at distal phalanx on 26.12.2021.

27. PW2 further stated that, at the time of his examination the petitioner walks with pain and limping, wasting of right arm and diffuse and swelling of right forearm, wasting of right thigh and diffuse and swelling of right leg is seen, surgical scars are seen over both right sided limbs.

Recent x- rays shows united fracture of both bones of right forearm with implants in situ are both sites, united fracture proximal tibia right with dhal plates in situ, amputation right great toe of distal phalanx level.
28. On the basis of entire evaluation of the disability of the petitioner, PW2 had opined that, total physical disability of 68% of both limbs and that of his whole body at 34%.

In support of his evidence produced clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.
29.
At the time of cross-examination of PW2, admitted that he is not treated doctor and fractures are well united.
Based on the documents he has assessed the physical disability.
This witness also denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
30. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 seems little bit exorbitant.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 22% instead of 34%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
31. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 28 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P8 for consideration.

On going through the said document,
the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 27.11.1992.
The accident occurred on 16.12.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 29 years.

To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '17' is to be taken into consideration.
32.

Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, he was working as a mason and getting an income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
He has not placed any documents to prove his income.

In such a situation,
as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.

It is pertinent to note that,
in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.

33. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled Krishna N vs Srinivas N on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65379443/
7 for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,000 X 12 X 17 X 22/100= Rs.6,73,200/-.
Loss of amenities;
34.

PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to fracture at right lower limb and amputation of right foot great toe, he find very difficult and painful to walk, sit, squat, climb and stairs, he cannot bear weight there is severe pain at fracture site.

On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a mason.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.
35. In connection with the future medication, PW2 has stated that petitioenr needs surgery for removal of implants in all four limbs which would cost around Rs.50,000/-.
But no estimation has been placed in this regard.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled to award compensation of Rs.30,000/-
under the head of future medical expenses.

36. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 60,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 45,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.1,65,965-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 20,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.6,73,200-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 30,000-00 7.
Future medication Rs. 30,000-00 Total Rs.10,24,165-00 37.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,24,165/- (Rupees ten lakh twenty four thousand one hundred and sixty five only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

sentences.text:
In support of his contention,
respondent No.2 has examined its company Legal Executive by name Aishwarya Rai S.M. as RW1.

But no convincing documents placed on record for consideration. Either to examine the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the independent witnesses who witnessed the alleged accident to prove that there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
40. Hence, it is clear that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-51-MF- 4328.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
41. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 12.2.2021 to 11.2.2022.
Same has been reflected in Ex.R1 placed by RW1.
The alleged accident had taken place on 16.12.2021.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
42.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,24,165/- (Rupees ten lakh twenty four thousand one hundred and sixty five only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The compensation awarded to the future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.

under the head of future medical expenses.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,24,165/- (Rupees ten lakh twenty four thousand one hundred and sixty five only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.3:
42.
In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,24,165/- (Rupees ten lakh twenty four thousand one hundred and sixty five only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The compensation awarded to the future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
